page: Amazon Web Services r5b.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Compute is delivered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs via two threads per core. The instance provides 64.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, representing an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with the instance, and it operates with a baseline network speed of 2 Gbps without dedicated graphics accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight solid memory subsystems alongside moderate computational throughput. Memory bandwidth measures 44.25 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 32.96 GB/sec for large-block writes. This supports operations such as in-memory data management, where Redis achieves 6.89 million SET operations per second, and static web serving reaches 7.1 GB/sec throughput. In contrast, CPU benchmarks reflect modest single-core performance, scoring 1116.0 in Geekbench and 1282.19 in stress-ng, both falling into the lower quartile.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the prioritization of memory capacity over high-frequency single-thread execution. Workloads requiring intense serial processing or heavy machine learning inference show reduced efficiency, evidenced by 7B model generation throughput of 6.79 tokens per second. Consequently, this configuration offers high resource efficiency for memory-bound tasks such as distributed caching, relational and in-memory database management, ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency web backends.
description: Amazon Web Services r5b.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. Running on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores at 3.1 GHz, complemented by 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory. This architecture provides an 8.0 GB per-vCPU memory allocation ratio without local storage or hardware accelerators, supported by a 2 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark testing reveals strong memory subsystem throughput, reaching 6.89 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.1 GB/sec static web serving throughput, offset by lower-tier single-threaded CPU scores. The resource profile provides balanced efficiency for memory-intensive requirements, making the instance suitable for distributed caches, in-memory databases, data pipelines, and general web serving workloads needing high memory capacity.
